Content: “Peter the Great was allowed to engage several English engineers into his service, as he had done in Holland; but, over and above engineers, he engaged likewise some mathematicians, which he would not so easily have found in Amsterdam. Ferguson, a Scotchman, an excellent geometrician, entered into his service, and was the `text(first)` person who brought arithmetic into use in the exchequer in Russia, where before that time, they made use only of the Tartarian method of reckoning, with balls strung upon a wire [an abacus]... He took with him `text(two)` young students from a mathematical school, and this was the beginning of the marine academy... Peter made himself proficient in astronomy, [and] he perfectly well understood the motions of the heavenly bodies, as well as the laws of gravitation, by which they are directed. This force, now so evidently demonstrated, and before the time of the great Newton so little known, by which all the planets gravitate towards each other, and which retain them in their orbits, had already become familiar to a sovereign of Russia, while other countries amused themselves with imaginary theories, and, in Galileo's nation, `text(one)` set of ignorant persons ordered others, as ignorant, to believe the earth to be immovable.”
Copyright: Voltaire, History of the Russian Empire Under Peter the Great, `text(1759)`, discussing Tsar Peter I's Grand Embassy, which traveled to western Europe at the end of the `text(seventeenth century)`
